text:
emily.w: Quick sync — we need a pragmatic backstop/shim strategy for v2 route incompatibilities. goal: let customers opt-in to v2 features while giving a safety net for critical v1 behaviors. thoughts?

raj.p: +1. want something low-friction for customers on large contracts. main asks: header-based opt-in, per-route fallbacks, and a clear deprecation policy. :thumbsup: 

samir.k: Agree. We should map the failure modes: (1) tool calling payload shape changes, (2) structured output schema strictness, (3) embedding dimensionality/behavior, (4) subtle tokenization/stop-sequence differences. Each needs different mitigations.

maria.t: For tool calling specifically, can we support a compatibility header that forces v1-style 'tool' envelope? e.g. `X-Redwood-Compat: v1-tool-envelope` so runtime can translate on the fly.

raj.p: That header idea is good. Also add a per-customer config in Dedicated/Private to pin route compatibility. Hosted customers can set via header or route policy in console.

emily.w: Concrete proposal draft: 1) Header opt-in flags for escape hatches (tool-envelope, relaxed-structured-output, v1-tokenization). 2) Runtime translation layers for tool-envelope -> v2 internal format. 3) Canary for each shim with telemetry gating. 4) Clear launch gates + sunset timeline.

samir.k: Implementation note: translation for tool-envelope is doable but will add ~20-40ms p95 in worst cases unless we special-case routing. Could make it an explicit opt-in to avoid perf regressions by default.

infra-bot: deploy plan: feature-flag gates + rollout to staging -> canary region -> global. canary windows default 48h.

maria.t: Example shim header payload (very small):
```
POST /v2/chat/completions HTTP/1.1
Host: api.redwood.ai
X-Redwood-Compat: v1-tool-envelope,relaxed-structured-output
Authorization: Bearer ...
Content-Type: application/json

{ "model": "rwx-3", "messages": [...], "tools": [{"name":"search","args":{...}}] }
```
runtime will detect header and perform translation.

raj.p: For launch gates we should require: a) telemetry shows <1% error/regression across top 10 customers during canary, b) perf P95 impact <10% for simple text workloads, c) docs/migration guide published and one customer migration validated.

emily.w: Deprecation timeline suggestion: announce shim availability at v2 GA, start 12 month overlap where both v1 and shimmed v2 routes supported. After 6 months deprecate new v1 features (no new betas), after 12 months start soft-sunset warnings, 18 months enforced sunset for hosted. Dedicated/private customers can extend via support contract.

samir.k: Need an exceptions matrix: short-lived critical customers can get extended compatibility windows, but we require a remediation plan and migration owner. Also add automatic opt-out telemetry if shim hides regression.

maria.t: UX: Console -> Route settings -> Compatibility -> toggle header-less migration mode (console sets a route policy so customers don't need to modify clients). Good for large fleet migrations.

raj.p: Questions: 1) Do we try to auto-detect v1 payloads and apply shims transparently? 2) How many shims do we ship day-1?

emily.w: Answers: 1) Prefer explicit opt-in for day-1 to avoid accidental masking of regressions. We can prototype auto-detect later. 2) Ship two critical shims day-1: tool-envelope and relaxed-structured-output. Embeddings/ rerank quirks are day-2, tokenization are last resort.

infra-bot: note: telemetry hooks required: per-shim error rates, latency delta, shim-translation failures, and a mapping from customer->shim usage.

samir.k: Migration guide outline we should prepare: checklist (client header update or console toggle), test-suite hints (golden prompts), evaluation criteria (quality/regression thresholds), rollback steps.

emily.w: I'll draft the product spec and migration playbook. Owners: emily.w (product lead), samir.k (runtime impact/engineering), raj.p (customer prioritization), maria.t (UX + docs). Action items: 1) samir: rough cost/perf estimate for two shims by EOD Thursday. 2) infra: stub feature-flag + telemetry hooks by next Tuesday. 3) emily: draft public migration FAQ and proposed timeline by next week.

raj.p: Sounds good. One more ask — include a short list of 5 high-traffic customers we should invite to early canary (PM to coordinate).

emily.w: noted. I'll ping specific PMs and schedule a 30m sync tomorrow. Thanks all. :calendar:
